overview: Group Theory me GATE do cheezein baar-baar test karta hai: (1) diya gaya (Set, Operation) pair Semigroup/Monoid/Group/Abelian-Group hai ya nahi — ek fixed 4-point checklist se, (2) Lagrange's theorem based subgroup-order questions.
whyItMatters: 2018 se har saal continuously poocha ja raha hai — bahut recent-active P1 topic. Structure-identification pattern (closure/associative/identity/inverse) ek fixed, mechanical checklist hai — practice se bahut fast ho jaata hai.
coreConcept: Algebraic structure = (Set, Binary Operation). GATE 4 levels test karta hai: Semigroup (closure+associative) → Monoid (+identity) → Group (+inverse for every element) → Abelian Group (+commutative). Har level pichle level ka superset hai.
hinglishExplanation: Socho ek 'club' hai (the set) aur ek 'rule' hai do members ko combine karne ka (the operation). Closure = combine karne se result bhi club ke andar hi rahe (bahar na chala jaaye). Associative = grouping matter na kare ((a*b)*c = a*(b*c)). Identity = ek 'neutral' member ho jo kisi ko change na kare. Inverse = har member ka ek 'undo partner' ho jo combine karne par neutral de de. Commutative = order matter na kare (a*b = b*a).
formalDefinition: (G,*) is a Group if: (1) Closure: a,b∈G ⟹ a*b∈G. (2) Associativity: (a*b)*c = a*(b*c). (3) Identity: ∃e∈G such that a*e=e*a=a ∀a. (4) Inverse: ∀a∈G, ∃a⁻¹∈G such that a*a⁻¹=a⁻¹*a=e. Abelian additionally requires a*b=b*a ∀a,b.
importantProperties: Group = Monoid + every element has an inverse.
Lagrange's Theorem: order of any SUBGROUP divides the order of the GROUP. This is the single most-tested fact in this topic.
Every group of prime order p is cyclic and has ONLY two subgroups: {e} and itself (no proper nontrivial subgroups) — direct Lagrange consequence.
A cyclic group of order n has exactly one subgroup for each divisor of n.
Identity element and inverses in a group are always UNIQUE.

formulas.lagrangeTheorem: |H| divides |G| for any subgroup H of group G.
formulas.cosetPartition: Left cosets of H in G all have size |H| and partition G — hence |G| = |H| × (number of cosets, i.e. the index [G:H]).
formulas.cyclicGroupSubgroups: A cyclic group of order n has exactly one subgroup of order d, for every divisor d of n.

keyPropertiesAndIdentities: If a*a = e for every element a (every element is its own inverse), the group MUST be abelian — a classic 'prove abelian' GATE question.
A group of even order MUST have at least one element of order 2 (i.e., some a≠e with a*a=e) — Cauchy's theorem consequence, tested directly.
The intersection of two subgroups is always a subgroup; the UNION of two subgroups is generally NOT a subgroup (unless one contains the other).
commonPitfalls: Checking closure/associativity but forgetting to verify EVERY element has an inverse WITHIN the set (not just that an inverse formula exists in general).
Assuming commutativity is required for a 'Group' — it's only required for ABELIAN group, plain groups need not be commutative.
Assuming a subset that is 'closed' under the operation is automatically a subgroup — it also needs identity and inverses within that subset.
For 'largest proper subgroup' questions, forgetting that the answer must be the LARGEST divisor of |G| that is STRICTLY less than |G|.
standardTechniques: For structure-identification: run the 4-point checklist in order (closure → associative → identity → inverse → commutative) and stop as soon as one fails, naming the highest level reached.

For subgroup-order questions: list ALL divisors of |G|, that's your set of POSSIBLE subgroup orders (Lagrange gives necessary, not sufficient, condition — but GATE mostly tests the necessary-condition direction).
For 'largest proper subgroup': find the largest divisor of |G| that is strictly less than |G| itself — for |G|=prime, this is always 1 (only trivial subgroup).
